S-EE-001.cause: Missing or insufficient authentication and validation of external entities
S-EE-001.attack: Attacker impersonates a trusted external entity by sending forged requests, bypassing identity checks, or reusing stolen credentials

S-P-001.threat: Unauthorized process access via identity spoofing
S-P-001.cause: Weak or missing authentication mechanisms for process access
S-P-001.attack: Attacker spoofs a legitimate identity to gain unauthorized access to a protected process

S-P-002.threat: Process spoofing via malicious process replacement
S-P-002.cause: Lack of process integrity verification or trust validation
S-P-002.attack: Attacker replaces a legitimate process with a malicious one using the same identifier or interface

S-P-003.cause: Improper session management or weak session binding
S-P-003.attack: Attacker takes over a valid user session by stealing or predicting session identifiers

T-P-001.threat: Tampering with process logic or configuration
T-P-001.cause: Insufficient integrity protection for code or configuration
T-P-001.attack: Attacker modifies process code or runtime configuration to alter intended behavior

T-P-002.attack: Attacker exploits memory vulnerabilities such as buffer overflows to manipulate process memory

T-DF-001.cause: Missing integrity protection on data flows
T-DF-001.attack: Attacker intercepts and modifies data in transit between components

T-DF-002.cause: Lack of mutual authentication or secure channel protection
T-DF-002.attack: Attacker positions themselves between communicating parties to intercept and alter transmitted data

T-DS-001.cause: Insufficient access control or integrity protection on storage
T-DS-001.attack: Attacker directly modifies stored data bypassing application-level controls

T-DS-002.cause: Improper input validation and query construction
T-DS-002.attack: Attacker injects malicious input (e.g., SQL) to manipulate or alter stored data

R-EE-001.cause: Lack of reliable logging and non-repudiation mechanisms
R-EE-001.attack: External entity denies having performed an action due to missing or insufficient audit trails

R-P-001.attack: Attacker performs actions that cannot be traced back due to missing or incomplete logs

R-P-002.cause: Lack of protection and integrity controls for logs
R-P-002.attack: Attacker modifies or deletes logs to hide evidence of malicious activity

R-DS-001.cause: Missing audit trail for data changes
R-DS-001.attack: Attacker modifies stored data without leaving traceable evidence

I-P-001.cause: Excessive information exposure in error handling
I-P-001.attack: Detailed error messages reveal sensitive system or internal information

I-P-002.cause: Lack of memory isolation or side-channel protections
I-P-002.attack: Attacker extracts sensitive data from process memory using side-channel techniques

I-DF-001.cause: Unencrypted or weakly protected communication channels
I-DF-001.attack: Attacker intercepts and reads sensitive data transmitted between components

I-DF-002.cause: Lack of traffic obfuscation or metadata protection
I-DF-002.attack: Attacker analyzes communication patterns to infer sensitive information

I-DS-001.cause: Weak access control mechanisms on storage
I-DS-001.attack: Attacker gains unauthorized read access to sensitive stored data

I-DS-002.cause: Improper handling of backups, logs, or temporary files
I-DS-002.attack: Attacker accesses sensitive data through unsecured backups or log files

D-P-001.cause: Improper input validation or error handling
D-P-001.attack: Attacker sends malformed input to trigger crashes or exceptions

D-P-002.cause: Lack of rate limiting or resource controls
D-P-002.attack: Attacker floods the process with requests to exhaust system resources

D-DF-001.attack: Attacker floods network channels to disrupt legitimate communication

D-DS-001.cause: Lack of quotas or storage limits
D-DS-001.attack: Attacker fills storage capacity to block legitimate operations

D-DS-002.cause: Inefficient query handling and lack of resource safeguards
D-DS-002.attack: Attacker executes expensive or long-running queries to lock database resources

E-P-001.cause: Improper input validation and privilege enforcement
E-P-001.attack: Attacker exploits input validation flaws to gain elevated privileges

E-P-002.attack: Attacker bypasses authorization controls to access restricted functionality

E-P-003.cause: Injection vulnerabilities or unsafe execution paths
E-P-003.attack: Attacker injects and executes malicious code within the process context

S-IF-001.cause: Lack of authentication for connected interfaces or devices
S-IF-001.attack: Attacker connects a malicious device impersonating a trusted hardware interface

T-IF-001.cause: Lack of physical protection and tamper resistance
T-IF-001.attack: Attacker manipulates hardware interfaces to alter device behavior or data

R-IF-001.cause: Missing logging for physical interface interactions
R-IF-001.attack: Attacker performs actions via physical interface that cannot be traced

I-IF-001.cause: Unprotected physical or debug interfaces enabling passive monitoring
I-IF-001.attack: Attacker extracts sensitive information using monitoring equipment or side-channel techniques

D-IF-001.cause: Lack of physical protection against deliberate disruption
D-IF-001.attack: Attacker damages or electrically disrupts interface to cause system failure

E-IF-001.cause: Exposed debug or privileged hardware interfaces without access controls
E-IF-001.attack: Attacker uses physical access to debug ports (e.g., JTAG, UART) to gain elevated privileges

E-IF-002.cause: Lack of secure boot or firmware integrity validation
E-IF-002.attack: Attacker manipulates firmware or hardware configuration to gain privileged control over the device
